title: Independent predicates: countable languages and continuum many types
summary: Infinitely many independent unary predicates give a complete theory with continuum many one-types, none isolated, and no prime or countable universal model.
abstract: How much can a countable list of yes-or-no questions tell us about one element? Every finite answer pattern can occur infinitely often, while complete answer lists range over all subsets of the natural numbers. We build two models of this simple theory, prove that every formula reduces to finite predicate and equality tests, and identify its complete one-types with those subsets. No single formula can fix all answers: changing an unmentioned coordinate always produces another type. The example shows why a countable language need not have only countably many types, and why a complete theory can have neither a prime model nor a countable model into which all its countable models embed elementarily.
